extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO (particularly those facing OED discipline), OED staff, and counsel handling USPTO disciplinary/resignation matters
extracted.subtask_description: Approval of an affidavit of resignation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and issuance of an order excluding a respondent from practice before the USPTO in trademark and other non-patent matters, with attendant publication, notice, and reinstatement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit elements shown in this case include: (1) consent is freely and voluntarily rendered and not the result of coercion or duress; (2) awareness of a pending USPTO investigation of alleged misconduct; (3) awareness that the OED Director is of the opinion that the respondent's conduct violated specified Disciplinary Rules (here cited as 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b) via 10.23(c)(5)); (4) an acknowledgement that, without admitting violations, for purposes of any reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 the OED Director will conclusively presume the investigation allegations are true and that the respondent could not have successfully defended against them; (5) that the respondent has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60 and the implications of consenting to exclusion; and (6) express consent to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in trademark and other non-patent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Director authority to accept affidavit and order exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has statutory and regulatory authority to approve an affidavit of resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited authority: 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27. This establishes the procedural power to accept resignation affidavits and impose exclusion from practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of exclusion — trademark and other non-patent law
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion on consent applies to the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the respondent 'shall be excluded on consent from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the Office' effective on the date of the Final Order. The notice reiterates that the respondent is not authorized to practice in patent matters before the Office (see 37 C.F.R. § 11.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent registration status under 37 C.F.R. § 11.5
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a practitioner is registered to practice patent matters is relevant to the scope of permitted practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order notes the respondent 'is not registered to practice before the Office' and cites 37 C.F.R. § 11.5 to explain that non-registered attorneys are not authorized to practice patent matters before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds constituting a violation — disbarment by a state bar
rubrics_metrics.description: Disbarment on ethical grounds by a state bar can be characterized as a violation of USPTO Disciplinary Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director was of the opinion that the respondent's conduct violated 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) by being disbarred on ethical grounds by the State Bar of California from the practice of law in that state. The order uses state bar disbarment as a basis for the disciplinary action under USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and § 11.27(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish the Final Order and give notice of public discipline to relevant entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific actions ordered: publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room (http://des.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp), publish a Notice of Exclusion on Consent in the Official Gazette, and give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner was admitted or formerly admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent excluded on consent must comply fully with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly commands: 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.' (Section 11.58 addresses limitations on practice and notice obligations attendant to consented exclusions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure and presumptions (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent applies for reinstatement, they must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 and the OED Director will apply specified presumptions for limited purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged that, on any reinstatement application under § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the limited purpose of making a determination concerning reinstatement, that (i) the allegations set forth in the investigation are true and (ii) the respondent could not have successfully defended himself against such allegations. The order also requires: 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Official Gazette notice of exclusion on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice must set out the respondent's identity, registration status, basis for exclusion, and reinstatement presumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example content in the published notice includes: respondent's name and location; statement that respondent is not registered to practice patent matters (37 C.F.R. § 11.5); that the affidavit was accepted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(b); facts that the respondent voluntarily submitted the affidavit while subject to a disciplinary investigation (37 C.F.R. § 11.22(a)); the OED Director's opinion regarding violations (citing 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23 and 10.23(c)(5)); and the acknowledgement about reinstatement presumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred to date and in carrying out the agreement are to be borne by the parties themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states: 'The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.'
